text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania has banned imports of livestock and animal products from Bulgaria due to a the spread of foot and mouth disease in the neighbouring country.
- The outgoing cabinet of Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu leaves behind a foreign debt worth $7.0 billion.

- According to government decision, Romanian refineries are scheduled to process 530,000 tonnes of crude oil from domestic production and 800,000 tonnes of imported crude in November, roughly the same amount they handled in October, when weather is a lot warmer.
ADEVARUL
- The gap between the official rate of the leu and its price at retail currency shops has widened to 29 percent.

- Allowing more banks to act as dealers on the foreign exchange market will cause rapid disasters on a short-term basis, Razvan Temesa, president of Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA says in an interview.
AZI
- Private sector holds 91.2 percent of of cattle numbers in Romania.

- Municipality of Transylvanian city of Brasov accepted a bid from Sira Invest SA Romanian investment company and U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers to launch municipal bonds worth $150 million in the international capital market, along with a private placement of $50 million.
LIBERTATEA
- Troubled Banca Dacia Felix SA will soon pay depositors who want to redeem their money. The central bank will help the move with a 250 billion lei credit.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Teodor Maghiar, vice-president of the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) and rector of the university in the western town of Oradea was photographed voting with 15 ballots in his hands. Local prosecution started penal investigation.
- The elections were free and resonable fair, said the OSCE observers at Romania's elections on Sunday.
- A centre coalition government would be profitable for Romania, said President Ion Iliescu.
ADEVARUL

- Not the victory of the opposition parties in Sunday's poll is suprising, but the size of the win, says an editorial on the parliamentary elections in which the ruling Party of Social Democracy was defeated by the Democratic Conevention.
- With half of the votes counted, the CDR dominates both parliament houses, says the newspaper publishing the preliminary results.
- Gheorghe Funar, head of National Unity Party, said he would not support President Ion Iliescu in the second round run-off.

- Under the headline "Romania's political map after the partial count of the votes", the newspaper presents preliminary results in the presidential and parliamentary poll in 25 counties including the capital Bucharest.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Only after November 17 (the second round run-off in the presidential polls) it can be talked about a real change in Romania, says Ion Cristoiu in an editorial.
- The newspaper publishes excerpts from a report by the European Media Institute on the electoral campaign.
- An IRSOP poll shows that 25 percent of the people who voted for the National Salvation Front in 1992, turned into ruling PDSR, have voted for the CDR in 1996.
ZIUA

- The interior ministry issued 100,000 identity papers to people who allegedly had lost the identity cards. The election law allows people to vote with the identity card or with the temporary valid paper. As many as 200 so called tourists had voted in a village in the Black Sea county of Constanta compared to only 190 local citizens.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Interpol announced that Romanian citizens had committed 110 crimes abroad this year.

- Alin Teodorescu, head of the IMAS polling institute said that "something had happened and explanations must be found" on the contradictory results of the exit polls conducted by his instiutute and the IRSOP institute.
LIBERTATEA
- An opposition government will not last longer than four months due to the very difficult situation in the country, said President Iliescu.
DIMINEATA

- "All the forces, all the energies for Iliescu president", reads a front-page headline saying that the main goal now is President Iliescu to be re-elected to ensure a balance and not give the whole power to the CDR. ($=3,409 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
